implementationContract: Game-side bot IMPLEMENTATION contract (the bot RUNTIME is C#, heuristic, NOT learned/RL): each scripted persona run MUST emit one standard telemetry summary + event stream conforming to the genre telemetry schema `3d-topdown-arena.telemetry.v1` (Wave-A: genre-packs/3d-topdown-arena/telemetry.json), and MUST stamp the summary's `persona` field with the persona id declared here (already a required, segmentable summary field in the telemetry seed — no schema change needed). Loomtide owns ONLY this contract + the deterministic `buildPersonaCohortReport` analysis; it does not run the bot. A persona's numbers may back a balance claim ONLY when `calibrated: true` with a `calibrationEvidence` pointer — the persona report flags every uncalibrated persona as a caveat about the BOT, never a game-balance claim.
note: Persona spread for the 3D top-down extraction-shooter / greed-loop quadrant (dogfood findings; plan §8 'Bots Tune Balance, Humans Judge Fun'). The persona spread — Timid / Balanced / Greedy / Reckless — is more useful than one 'average' bot: it exposes whether the loop supports safe extraction, moderate greed, and over-greed failure. INTENT is stated BEFORE any pass rate. HONEST CALIBRATION POSTURE: every persona here ships `calibrated: false` with `calibrationEvidence: null` — these envelope bands are placeholders DERIVED FROM THE DESIGN DOC, not yet calibrated against a real bot cohort. Calibrate each persona against a fixed run-set (set calibrated:true + a report pointer) BEFORE tuning the game around its outcomes. Envelope bands are bound BY NAME to telemetry summary fields (bankedValue/lostValue means; extraction/death rates over the `outcome` field) so the two schemas stay bound; a band naming a non-existent telemetry field is refused. Rate = fraction of the persona's runs whose `outcome` equals the given value.

personas.intent: Bank early and safely: grab modest loot and extract at the first safe opportunity, disengaging from any enemy contact. Optimizes for a completed extraction over total value. Expected to almost always extract with LOW banked value and low losses.

dials.name: lootGreedThreshold
dials.description: Carried loot value at which the bot stops collecting and heads to extract. Low for Timid — banks small.

dials.name: retreatHealthFraction
dials.description: Health fraction at which the bot breaks off and retreats. High for Timid — retreats early.

dials.name: extractTriggerValue
dials.description: Banked-value target that triggers an extraction attempt. Low for Timid.

dials.name: engagementRange
dials.description: Distance at which the bot will engage an enemy rather than avoid. Small for Timid — mostly avoids.

envelope.description: High extraction rate — Timid should bank almost every run.
Low mean banked value — extracts early with modest loot.
Low mean lost value — rarely dies carrying loot.

personas.intent: Weigh greed against risk: take moderate loot, then extract; disengage when health is low but hold position for a high-value pickup. Expected to show a MEANINGFUL success/failure spread — the loop's 'normal' player.

envelope.description: Moderate extraction rate — meaningful spread of success/failure.
Some lost value — takes real risk.

personas.intent: Chase high-value loot before extracting, accepting higher exposure for higher upside. Expected to create HIGHER banked upside AND higher death/loss risk than Balanced — over-greed should be punished by the economy, not by confusion.

dials.name: extractTriggerValue
dials.description: High banked-value extraction trigger — greedy for a big bank.

dials.name: engagementRange
dials.description: Wider engagement range — fights for loot.

envelope.description: Lower extraction rate than Balanced — over-commits.
Higher death rate — the cost of greed.
High mean banked value WHEN it extracts — the upside.
High mean lost value — dies carrying more.

personas.intent: Over-commit to loot and combat with little regard for extraction timing or health. Expected to USUALLY FAIL for LEGIBLE reasons (dies deep, carrying value it never banked) — a broken-over-committer used to probe whether failure is fair, NOT a reason to nerf the game.

dials.name: lootGreedThreshold
dials.description: Very high — almost never stops for extraction.

dials.name: extractTriggerValue
dials.description: Very high extraction trigger — rarely reached before death.

envelope.description: Low extraction rate — usually dies first.
High death rate — over-commits to failure.
Low mean banked value — rarely banks.
High mean lost value — dies carrying loot it never secured.
